transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-25 15:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Title: Staged traffic transition and fallbacks review - Fabricon pilot
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Benji (Redwood SE), Jordan (Fabricon Eng), Priya (Fabricon Product), Carlos (Fabricon SRE)
Shared links: Runbook draft: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/fabricon-canary (note: internal), Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.fabricon.example/d/abcd, Pilot metrics sheet: https://sheets.app/drive/fabricon-pilot-metrics

Summary (auto):
Discussed staged traffic shift plan for canary and A/B splits, rollback and fallback triggers, monitoring thresholds, and runbook steps for cutover. Agreed to dry-run canary on 2025-12-01; SE to finalize playbook and dashboards. Pricing/contract to be finalized by AE.

Topics:
- Canary percentages and stepping cadence
- Observability: metrics, alerts, dashboards
- Rollback conditions and automated fallbacks to hosted model tier
- Runbook ownership and dry-run schedule
- Data retention / logs and audit for compliance

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): Okay, thanks everyone for joining. Quick roll call — I see Jordan, Priya, Carlos — good. Intention for today is to walk the staged-traffic transition, make sure the canary thresholds and fallbacks make sense, and confirm next steps. Benji, do you want to kick us off with the runbook summary?

[01:12] Benji (Redwood SE): Yeah, sure. I put the latest playbook in the shared link — it's a step-by-step for the dry run and cutover. High level: start with 1% traffic for 30 minutes, check key metrics (5xx, 95th latency, token cost per req), then 5% for an hour, 25% for two hours, and then 100% if all gates pass. We included KV cache warm-up step — we call out prefix caching and cold-start ramps.

[02:45] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Quick question — when you say "KV cache warm-up" is that automatic for Redwood or do we need a pre-population script? In our tests we saw some cold-token latencies that spiked for first few requests.

[03:10] Benji (Redwood SE): Good call — we have automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts but we recommend a small prewarm job for stateful flows. The runbook includes a sample prewarm curl script under the prewarm section. I'll attach a one-click job you can run in your env to warm the cache. Also note: if you're on Dedicated we can do a persistent cache; for Hosted there's a short TTL.

[04:20] Priya (Fabricon Product): From product side, our success criteria are 95th latency under 400ms and error rate <0.5% during the canary. Is that realistic with your default batching settings?

[04:45] Benji (Redwood SE): 95th at 400ms depends on model and sequence length. On small assistant prompts we've hit ~220ms 95th on our dedicated pools with fine-tuned batching. For longer sequences (600 tokens) you're likely to see more. We recommended two levers: reduce batching max_window for the canary to prioritize latency, and pin to a smaller model variant if cost isn't critical. We can show a config diff for the canary run.

[06:05] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Do we need to change autoscale policies for the canary? Right now our autoscaler steps in at 60% CPU/GPU util and it takes about 3 minutes to add nodes. That's sort of slow for rapid traffic increases.

[06:32] Benji (Redwood SE): For canary we suggest pre-provisioning a small burst pool to avoid scale lag — set a dedicated pool with min nodes equal to expected peak for the step. The runbook includes an autoscale override snippet. Also you can do route-based throttling at the API gateway to control ramp.

[07:50] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): On monitoring, we need concrete alert rules we can plug into our PagerDuty. Can you share the exact Grafana panels and threshold exports?

[08:10] Benji (Redwood SE): Yep, the dashboard link in the notes has the panels and we exported an alerts.json — I'll drop that in the sheet. Key ones: 95th latency > 450ms for 5 min, error rate >0.5% for 5 min, token cost per minute deviates >20% from baseline. We also recommended an SLO burn rate check during the 25% step.

[09:25] Priya (Fabricon Product): I also want to confirm rollback policy. If the canary fails at 5% do we fully rollback to previous model or route to hosted low-cost fallback?

[09:45] Benji (Redwood SE): Both options are supported. Two patterns: instant full rollback to previous pinned model, or a gradual fallback to Redwood's hosted fallback tier for degraded capacity. The latter gives you degraded functionality but keeps availability. The runbook includes both flowcharts; we should pick one for the pilot. My recommendation is immediate rollback for safety and a secondary hosted fallback if rollback can't be completed fast.

[11:05] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Are there automated indicators for rollback? Like can we have an automated circuit-breaker on the gateway to switch routes if 5xx spikes?

[11:22] Benji (Redwood SE): Absolutely — we can integrate a circuit-breaker to swap routing policy. Redwood's routing supports per-route policies and thresholds, so it can re-route to the fallback model if errors exceed threshold for N minutes. That ties into the runbook step: trigger threshold -> circuit-breaker -> notify -> rollback.

[13:00] Alicia (Redwood AE): Quick commercial note — for Dedicated pilot we included a short-term burst capacity at no extra cost if the canary hits your SLA gates. That was in the draft SOW. Jordan, is that the model you expect to use?

[13:25] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Yes, we'd prefer Dedicated for predictable latencies but we need the VPC/private deployment check for compliance. Any blockers there?

[13:40] Benji (Redwood SE): Private deployment looks good; we've validated network rules with your infra team in the prior call. Small note: HSM/KMS integration for logs and audit is a separate workstream — we'll need your security contact to sign the network peering and KMS access plan.

[14:55] Priya (Fabricon Product): One more thing — during internal load tests we saw a weird token-cost spike when model fallbacks kicked in. Is that expected?

[15:12] Benji (Redwood SE): That can happen if fallback model has higher per-token cost or if caching isn't shared across variants. We can configure the routing to prefer a cheaper compatible variant rather than the most expensive hosted fallback. We'll document per-step expected token cost deltas in the pilot metrics sheet.

[17:00] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): For audit and logs: we require immutable audit trail for inference requests (headers, model version, user-id hash). Can Redwood provide request-level logs with retention 90 days?

[17:25] Benji (Redwood SE): Yes, we can export request logs to your S3 with customer-managed KMS and retention policy. For private deployments that's standard; for Hosted we have a managed logs export option — depends on plan. I'll confirm exact schema and include a sample export.

[19:10] Priya (Fabricon Product): About A/B testing — we discussed earlier wanting to test two prompt templates. How does the runbook manage A/B metric collection?

[19:30] Benji (Redwood SE): You can use route-level tagging to split traffic 50/50 and we capture labels in emitted metrics so you can compute A/B conversions. The canary runbook has a section for metric tagging and aggregation windows. We'll add example PromQL queries for conversion delta and statistical significance checks.

[21:00] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Any caveats about warm-start vs cold-start for A/B? We want to avoid bias where one arm is artificially slower because it's cold.

[21:20] Benji (Redwood SE): Good point — include a prewarm step for both arms, and don't measure until a stabilization window (we usually wait 10-15 minutes after prewarm). The runbook includes that gating.

[23:05] Alicia (Redwood AE): We should walk through the exact canary timeline aloud and confirm owners. Benji, read the steps and owners?

[23:20] Benji (Redwood SE): Step 0: Prewarm caches — Jordan (owner), run prewarm script and confirm metrics. Step 1: 1% for 30 min — Carlos to monitor alerts and escalate. Step 2: 5% for 1h — Priya product to validate correctness. Step 3: 25% for 2h — SRE and SE watch SLOs. Step 4: 100% cutover — Alicia to sign off and trigger final route. Rollback triggers: 95th latency > 450ms for 5m, error rate > 0.5% for 5m, or user-facing defect rate above defined threshold.

[25:40] Priya (Fabricon Product): For 25% step, what telemetry do we need to validate quality? We need sample outputs and manual review acceptance too.

[26:00] Benji (Redwood SE): We'll route a 1% sample of generated outputs to an internal secure review dashboard for manual QA during the 5% and 25% steps — sampling will be hashed and PII removed. That's in the runbook under QA sampling.

[27:30] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): One operational concern: can we simulate the rollback in staging so we know the exact time it takes? We don't want surprises during prod canary.

[27:52] Benji (Redwood SE): Yes, we recommend a dry-run in a staging mirror that simulates your gateway and traffic shape. The schedule item for 2025-12-01 is the dry-run. That will exercise rollback and circuit-breaker.

[29:10] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): On data privacy — if a request contains sensitive PII we need guaranteed redaction before logs leave our cluster. Will Redwood do that or do we redact upstream?

[29:35] Benji (Redwood SE): Upstream redaction is recommended for PII-sensitive fields; we can also configure a server-side preprocessor step, but that adds latency and complexity. We'll include recommended regex filters in the runbook.

[31:00] Priya (Fabricon Product): Legal requested SOC2 evidence and architecture diagram showing log flow. Is that in the security pack you shared?

[31:20] Alicia (Redwood AE): Yes we shared a security bundle earlier — I will re-send the SOC2 report and the architecture diagram. Note that for Private deployments we can offer extra attestations.

[33:45] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): Benchmarks — in your earlier email Benji included a spreadsheet with median/95th under different loads. Can you summarize expected 95th at 25% traffic for our baseline model?

[34:05] Benji (Redwood SE): Based on your traffic profile from last week (avg payload 180 tokens, seq len ~320) we estimate 95th at ~350-420ms on Dedicated with our optimized kernels and batching tailored for throughput. I'll add a column in the pilot metrics sheet that shows expected ranges per step.

[36:00] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): A quick note on canary percentage cadence — are we confident that 1% to 5% jump is safe enough? Any reason to use 2.5% then 10%?

[36:20] Benji (Redwood SE): It's configurable. We chose 1->5->25 as practical but you can do finer steps (1->2.5->5->10->25) if you want extra caution. That will lengthen the total window but is safer for customer-facing flows.

[38:10] Priya (Fabricon Product): On the dashboard side, can we get a per-customer tenant breakdown so product can see any variance by segment?

[38:30] Benji (Redwood SE): Yes, if your requests include a tenant_id we can tag metrics and build tenant-level panels. We do that for multi-tenant pilots frequently.

[40:05] Alicia (Redwood AE): Okay let's capture the decisions: dry-run on 12/01, owners for each step as Benji outlined, runbook finalization by 11/28, pricing/contract by 11/27. Any objections?

[40:35] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): No objections. One ask though: can you include a fallback that routes to a cheaper variant rather than the most expensive hosted fallback? That helps our cost predictability.

[40:55] Benji (Redwood SE): Yup we'll configure routing preferences and include expected per-step token-cost deltas in the sheet.

[42:10] Priya (Fabricon Product): Also please include a checklist for legal compliance signoffs prior to production cutover.

[42:30] Alicia (Redwood AE): I'll own legal coordination. I'll circulate the checklist and tag your security contact.

[44:00] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): One more operational detail — is the rollback instantaneous or does it take some time to spin down cache state? If we rollback to previous model, will the KV cache be compatible?

[44:20] Benji (Redwood SE): Cache compatibility depends on model architecture and tokenizer alignment. In some cases cache warm-up may be needed; that's why we include a rapid fallback path and prewarm script to re-populate cache if needed. We'll document expected cold-cache penalty in the runbook.

[46:10] Alicia (Redwood AE): Great — any final risks from Fabricon side?

[46:22] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Main risk is autoscale lag and cache cold starts. We'll test both in the dry-run.

[46:40] Priya (Fabricon Product): From product risk: user-visible degradation during the 25% ramp if we don't catch issues quickly. We'll be on standby for manual rollback.

[47:00] Benji (Redwood SE): We'll set up a dedicated Slack channel for real-time alerts and an incident bridge link in the runbook for the dry run. I'll include how to trigger it (step-by-step).

[48:15] Alicia (Redwood AE): Ok let's recap verbally — decisions and owners (quick): Dry run 12/01 (Jordan+Benji), Runbook finalization by 11/28 (Benji), Pricing & SOW 11/27 (Alicia), Grafana alert export and dashboards by 11/27 (Benji), Legal checklist by 11/27 (Alicia).

[49:05] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Sounds good. Could you also add a performance test to validate SLOs at 25% earlier in staging?

[49:20] Benji (Redwood SE): Yes we'll schedule a staging perf test during next week and share results in the metrics sheet.

[50:45] Priya (Fabricon Product): One last note — please ensure that sampled outputs for QA are PII-sanitized before appearing in dashboards. We've had privacy flags internally.

[51:05] Benji (Redwood SE): Understood — we'll sanitize at ingestion and only provide hashed IDs.

[52:30] Alicia (Redwood AE): Thanks all. I'll follow up with the SOW and security bundle, Benji will update runbook and dashboards, Jordan will prepare prewarm and traffic profiles. We'll reconvene after the dry-run. Any final words?

[53:05] Carlos (Fabricon SRE): None from me. Thanks.

[53:20] Jordan (Fabricon Eng): Thanks everyone.

[53:30] Alicia (Redwood AE): Great — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription imperfections: some brand and acronyms transcribed as separate letters (V P C, K V cache), occasional speaker mislabels in autogenerated output, filler words preserved.
